description: The image is titled "Diagram 2.32 Wall type 3 – external cavity wall with internal timber wall". It is a three-dimensional cross-section showing the corner of a building wall assembly. The outermost layer consists of a brick wall. A gap, or cavity, separates this from the inner block wall. At the top of the cavity, a label reads "Cavity stop", pointing to a short block bridging the outer wall and the inner block. Another label, "Mineral wool pad", points to a pad within the inner block wall. Further inside, set back from the main wall structure, is a framed partition. A label at the bottom left reads "Internal timber wall", pointing to a timber stud of this framework. A label at the bottom right reads "Sealed joints", pointing to the joint where the timber wall meets the inner block wall. The drawing is a line drawing showing the spatial relationship between the external masonry, the insulation, and the internal timber partition.
